sources.title: WASH National Adaptation Plan for Uganda (2026-2030)
sources.organization: Republic of Uganda, Ministry of Water and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: WASH sector adaptation plan for 2026-2030; vulnerability analysis combines hazard and service indicators from cited datasets of varying dates.
sources.methodology: Plan combines a WASH vulnerability assessment, hazard mapping and district service indicators.
sources.limitations: Inputs include OPM's 2019 atlas; the plan is not an impact evaluation.

sources.title: Conducting and Developing the Climate Change and Vulnerability Assessment (CCVA) Framework Report for Kampala Capital City Authority
sources.organization: Republic of Uganda, Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA)
sources.temporal_coverage: Kampala assessment published June 2025; combines historical climate data, projections, GIS and stakeholder evidence across five divisions.
sources.methodology: GIS and climate/social datasets, 400 household surveys, 20 focus groups and 30 interviews used purposive stratified sampling.
sources.limitations: Vulnerable-area sampling is not population-representative; some local narratives cite older studies.

sources.title: Pastoral conflict on the greener grass? Exploring the climate-conflict nexus in the Karamoja Cluster
sources.organization: Rebecca Navarro, Lamis Saleh and Evelyne Owino; International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction; abstract hosted by PreventionWeb
geographic_coverage: Karamoja Cluster, cross-border; country-level findings not disaggregated
sources.temporal_coverage: Abstract describes conflict dynamics in 2018-2023 and an empirical environmental-variable analysis.
sources.methodology: Abstract describes informant interviews and empirical linkage/prediction analysis using environmental variables and conflict data.
sources.limitations: Only the abstract was readable; the journal full text was inaccessible, and cross-border cluster findings are not disaggregated for Uganda.

claims.locator: Printed p. 34 (PDF p. 49), Table 6, Exposure analysis for flooding.
claims.paraphrase: The plan reports over 80% of populations in Katakwi, Otuke, Kitgum, Nwoya, Sembabule and Kalungu exposed to floods at least one metre deep.
claims.limitations: Hazard exposure, not losses or attribution.

claims.locator: Printed p. 35 (PDF p. 50), Table 7, Exposure analysis for landslides.
claims.paraphrase: The plan reports over 80% population exposure to landslides in Bulambuli, Kapchorwa, Bukwo, Kween, Kisoro and Rubanda; over 60% of homes are exposed in five of these districts.
In Karamoja, perennial surface water is scarce and valley dams cannot meet livestock needs; basic drinking-water access is 38%, compared with 97% in Kampala.

claims.locator: Printed p. 42 (PDF p. 58), Box 5, Climate Change and Mobility impacts on WASH.
claims.paraphrase: The plan projects internal climate mobility may concentrate in southwestern Uganda by 2050, pressuring host-area water and WASH systems.
claims.scenario: GCCM 2024 high-emissions/unequal-development scenario; up to 5.1 million internal movers.
claims.limitations: Conditional projection, not observed movement or conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The plan says host-migrant water pressure could fuel conflict over water allocation.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed pp. 4-5 (PDF pp. 5-6), Key Findings and Highlights.
claims.paraphrase: KCCA identifies recurring floods in low-lying informal Bwaise, Katwe and Namuwongo; Nakawa, Makindye and Kawempe score highest on its division vulnerability index.
claims.limitations: The index combines socioeconomic indicators; this is not an FCV classification.

claims.locator: Printed p. 82 (PDF p. 83), section 6.3.2, Kawempe Division drought narrative.
claims.paraphrase: KCCA links repeated 10-day dry spells in Kawempe to crop failures and unsafe-water reliance; long queues at communal water points are said to fuel social tension.
claims.limitations: The narrative cites UNMA 2019; it does not estimate a causal effect or conflict incidence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report says queues at communal water points during drought-related shortages fuel social tension.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Printed p. 82 (PDF p. 83), Kawempe drought narrative.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 97-98 (PDF pp. 98-99), section 8.1, Table 9 and accompanying analysis.
claims.paraphrase: KCCA reports flood-resistant housing and drainage among more consistently adopted household measures in Kawempe, Lubaga and Nakawa; stormwater retention adoption was low, especially in Central and Nakawa.
claims.limitations: Reported household practices are not an independently verified effectiveness evaluation.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 6), Community Awareness Gaps; methods printed p. 19 (PDF p. 20).
claims.paraphrase: In KCCA's 400-person household survey, 30% knew of climate policies and more than half considered them ineffective.
claims.limitations: The purposively stratified survey is not a citywide population-prevalence estimate.

claims.locator: PreventionWeb article record, abstract paragraphs 1-2; journal DOI landing page was inaccessible.
claims.paraphrase: For 2018-2023, the Karamoja Cluster study says crisis policies restricted transhumant pastoral mobility, leaving communities more exposed to climate impacts.
geographies: Karamoja Cluster (cross-border; Uganda component not disaggregated)
claims.limitations: Abstract-only cross-border finding; no Uganda-specific effect or district result is reported.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The abstract says crisis policies restricted pastoral mobility and left communities exposed to climate impacts.

claims.paraphrase: The abstract reports vegetation associated with lower conflict broadly, but cluster conflict peaked during scarcity following periods of resource abundance.
geographies: Karamoja Cluster (cross-border; Uganda component not disaggregated)
claims.limitations: Abstract-only cluster result; association and prediction do not establish causation or Uganda-specific patterns.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The abstract reports conflict peaks after resource abundance when environmental scarcity followed.

access_audit.locator: Complete 113-page WASH National Adaptation Plan; printed pp. 12, 27, 34-35 and 42, including Boxes 3 and 5 and Tables 6-7.
access_audit.notes: Publisher-hosted PDF body was directly read. Local exposure tables cite OPM 2019; mobility projection is attributed by the plan to Global Centre for Climate Mobility 2024.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate open licence verified; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Complete 197-page KCCA assessment; executive summary, printed pp. 18-20, 82, 97-98 and 107 reviewed.
access_audit.notes: Direct PDF body read. Method reports 400 household surveys, 20 FGDs and 30 KIIs with purposive stratified sampling; local narrative cites older underlying data in places.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate open licence verified; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: PreventionWeb record, publication details and abstract paragraphs 1-3.

access_audit.reuse_terms: Abstract paraphrased briefly; article reuse terms not independently verified.

access_audit.locator: Journal publisher DOI landing page for the 2025 article.
access_audit.notes: Redirected to an inaccessible Elsevier page; no full-text-only findings were used.

access_audit.locator: FAO SHARP+ cattle-corridor resilience endline factsheet linked from the FAO release page.
access_audit.notes: Repository request returned 403. The accessible FAO release page only confirmed the 2018/2025 assessment design and eight-district scope; no inaccessible factsheet findings were used.

access_audit.locator: FAO release page body, paragraphs dated 12 February 2026.
access_audit.notes: Page says the endline factsheet presents results across eight cattle-corridor districts and 23 modules, but the accessible text contains no district names or substantive results; not used for findings.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Brief factual page description only; no separate licence verified.

search_audit.query: Uganda district climate vulnerability drought floods local government report 2024 2025 northern Karamoja official
search_audit.outcome: Read the 2026 WASH NAP district hazard/service tables and the full 2025 KCCA division/neighborhood assessment; found concrete Karamoja, flood- and landslide-district, and Kampala informal-settlement findings.

search_audit.query: Uganda climate conflict security climate change pastoralism Karamoja conflict primary research report district
search_audit.outcome: The WASH NAP states a conditional climate-mobility/water-allocation conflict pathway; KCCA links Kawempe drought-related shared-water queues to social tension. A 2025 Karamoja Cluster study abstract reports mobility restrictions and conflict-resource dynamics but is not Uganda-disaggregated.

search_audit.query: Uganda conflict insecurity prevents climate adaptation response access drought floods project northern districts report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected source documented conflict or insecurity blocking a named local climate-adaptation activity or response. This is a search gap, not evidence that such constraints are absent.

search_audit.query: Uganda local resilience capacity district adaptation pastoral communities climate response outcomes 2024 2025 UN government report
search_audit.outcome: KCCA reports household coping/adaptation responses and awareness gaps; the WASH NAP documents district service-capacity differences and proposed 2026-2030 actions. FAO announced a 2018/2025 cattle-corridor endline assessment, but its linked findings PDF was inaccessible.

gaps: The 2025 Karamoja Cluster article was available only as an abstract; it reports cross-border findings without Uganda-specific district attribution.

The 2026 WASH NAP's exposure indices rely substantially on the Office of the Prime Minister's 2019 hazard atlas; its local exposure percentages are not observed event-loss or climate-attribution estimates.
The FAO cattle-corridor endline factsheet repository link returned 403; the accessible release page omitted district names and substantive results.
No inspected source documented insecurity or violence preventing a named Ugandan climate-adaptation activity; that remains an evidence-search gap.
